# synth-verify - Formal Verification for Synth Compiler

Formal verification infrastructure for the Synth WebAssembly-to-ARM compiler using SMT-based translation validation.

## Overview

This crate provides:

- **SMT-based translation validation**using Z3 SMT solver
- **Formal semantics**for WebAssembly and ARM operations
- **Property-based testing**framework with proptest
- **Automated verification**of synthesis rules

## Architecture

```
synth-verify/
├── wasm_semantics.rs      # WASM → SMT encoding (25+ operations)
├── arm_semantics.rs       # ARM → SMT encoding (processor state model)
├── translation_validator.rs # Equivalence prover (Alive2-inspired)
└── properties.rs          # Property-based tests (50+ properties)
```
## Usage

### Verifying a Synthesis Rule

```
use ;
use ;
// Create Z3 context
let ctx = create_z3_context;
let validator = new;
// Define a synthesis rule
let rule = SynthesisRule ;
// Verify the rule
match validator.verify_rule
```
### Batch Verification

```
// Verify multiple rules
let rules = vec!;
let results = validator.verify_rules;
for  in results
```
### Property-Based Testing

```
use CompilerProperties;
use *;
proptest!
```
## Verification Approach

### Translation Validation

For each synthesis rule `WASM_OP → ARM_OPS`, we prove:

```
∀inputs. ⟦WASM_OP⟧(inputs) = ⟦ARM_OPS⟧(inputs)
```
Using SMT solver:

- Create symbolic inputs
- Encode WASM semantics: `φ_wasm`
- Encode ARM semantics: `φ_arm`
- Assert: `φ_wasm ≠ φ_arm`
- Check satisfiability:
- **UNSAT**→ Proven correct
- **SAT**→ Counterexample found
- **UNKNOWN**→ Timeout

### Example: ADD Verification

```
; Symbolic inputs
(declare-const a (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-const b (_ BitVec 32))
; WASM: i32.add
(define-fun wasm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; ARM: ADD R0, R0, R1
(define-fun arm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; Prove equivalence
(assert (not (= wasm-add arm-add)))
(check-sat)  ; Returns: unsat → Proven!
```
## Verified Operations

| Operation | Status | Method |
|---|---|---|
| i32.add | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.sub | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.mul | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_s | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_u | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.and | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.or | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.xor | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.shl | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_u | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_s | ⚠ Partial | Complex |

## Dependencies

### Required

- **z3**- Z3 SMT solver Rust bindings (v0.12)
- **synth-synthesis**- Synthesis rules and operations
- **proptest**- Property-based testing

### System Requirements

Z3 requires either:

- System installation: `libz3-dev`or`z3`package
- Static linking: Built automatically (requires C++ compiler)

For development without Z3:

```
# Skip tests that require Z3
```
## Testing

```
# Run all tests (requires Z3)
# Run specific test suites
# Property-based testing with more cases
PROPTEST_CASES=10000
```
## Performance

- Verification time: 50-500ms per rule (SMT solving)
- Memory usage: ~50MB (Z3 context)
- Scalability: Linear in number of rules

## Limitations

- **Shift operations**: Modulo handling complex for SMT
- **Control flow**: Branch verification requires extended modeling
- **Memory operations**: Requires memory model formalization
- **Floating point**: Not yet supported

## Future Work

### Phase 1: Complete SMT Coverage

- Shift operation verification
- Control flow (branches, conditions)
- Memory operations (load/store)

### Phase 2: Optimization Verification

- DCE, constant folding, CSE correctness
- Loop optimization soundness
- Register allocation preservation

### Phase 3: Mechanized Proofs

- Port to Coq proof assistant
- Machine-checked correctness
- Certified synthesis rule library

## References

- **Alive2**: Automated LLVM verification (Lopes et al., PLDI 2021)
- **CompCert**: Verified C compiler (Leroy, POPL 2006)
- **VeriISLE**: Verified instruction selection (Nandi et al., PLDI 2020)
- **Z3**: Efficient SMT solver (de Moura & Bjørner, TACAS 2008)

## License

Dual-licensed under Apache-2.0 OR MIT

## Authors

PulseEngine Team

---

- **Automated verification**of synthesis rules

## Architecture

```
synth-verify/
├── wasm_semantics.rs      # WASM → SMT encoding (25+ operations)
├── arm_semantics.rs       # ARM → SMT encoding (processor state model)
├── translation_validator.rs # Equivalence prover (Alive2-inspired)
└── properties.rs          # Property-based tests (50+ properties)
```

### Verifying a Synthesis Rule

```

```

## Verification Approach

### Translation Validation

For each synthesis rule `WASM_OP → ARM_OPS`, we prove:

```
∀inputs. ⟦WASM_OP⟧(inputs) = ⟦ARM_OPS⟧(inputs)
```
Using SMT solver:

- Create symbolic inputs
- Encode WASM semantics: `φ_wasm`
- Encode ARM semantics: `φ_arm`
- Assert: `φ_wasm ≠ φ_arm`
- Check satisfiability:
- **UNSAT**→ Proven correct
- **SAT**→ Counterexample found
- **UNKNOWN**→ Timeout

### Example: ADD Verification

```
; Symbolic inputs
(declare-const a (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-const b (_ BitVec 32))
; WASM: i32.add
(define-fun wasm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; ARM: ADD R0, R0, R1
(define-fun arm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; Prove equivalence
(assert (not (= wasm-add arm-add)))
(check-sat)  ; Returns: unsat → Proven!
```
## Verified Operations

| Operation | Status | Method |
|---|---|---|
| i32.add | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.sub | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.mul | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_s | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_u | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.and | ✓ Proven | SMT |

| i32.xor | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.shl | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_u | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_s | ⚠ Partial | Complex |

### Required

- **z3**- Z3 SMT solver Rust bindings (v0.12)
- **synth-synthesis**- Synthesis rules and operations
- **proptest**- Property-based testing

### System Requirements

Z3 requires either:

- System installation: `libz3-dev`or`z3`package
- Static linking: Built automatically (requires C++ compiler)

For development without Z3:

```
# Skip tests that require Z3
```
## Testing

```
# Run all tests (requires Z3)
# Run specific test suites
# Property-based testing with more cases
PROPTEST_CASES=10000
```
## Performance

- Verification time: 50-500ms per rule (SMT solving)
- Memory usage: ~50MB (Z3 context)
- Scalability: Linear in number of rules

## Limitations

- **Shift operations**: Modulo handling complex for SMT
- **Control flow**: Branch verification requires extended modeling
- **Memory operations**: Requires memory model formalization
- **Floating point**: Not yet supported

## Future Work

### Phase 1: Complete SMT Coverage

- Shift operation verification
- Control flow (branches, conditions)
- Memory operations (load/store)

### Phase 2: Optimization Verification

- DCE, constant folding, CSE correctness
- Loop optimization soundness
- Register allocation preservation

### Phase 3: Mechanized Proofs

- Port to Coq proof assistant
- Machine-checked correctness
- Certified synthesis rule library

## References

- **Alive2**: Automated LLVM verification (Lopes et al., PLDI 2021)
- **CompCert**: Verified C compiler (Leroy, POPL 2006)
- **VeriISLE**: Verified instruction selection (Nandi et al., PLDI 2020)

- Memory usage: ~50MB (Z3 context)
- Scalability: Linear in number of rules

## Limitations

- **Shift operations**: Modulo handling complex for SMT
- **Control flow**: Branch verification requires extended modeling
- **Memory operations**: Requires memory model formalization
- **Floating point**: Not yet supported

(declare-const a (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-const b (_ BitVec 32))
; WASM: i32.add
(define-fun wasm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; ARM: ADD R0, R0, R1
(define-fun arm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; Prove equivalence
(assert (not (= wasm-add arm-add)))
(check-sat)  ; Returns: unsat → Proven!
```
## Verified Operations

| Operation | Status | Method |
|---|---|---|
| i32.add | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.sub | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.mul | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_s | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_u | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.and | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.or | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.xor | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.shl | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_u | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_s | ⚠ Partial | Complex |

- **z3**- Z3 SMT solver Rust bindings (v0.12)
- **synth-synthesis**- Synthesis rules and operations
- **proptest**- Property-based testing

- System installation: `libz3-dev`or`z3`package
- Static linking: Built automatically (requires C++ compiler)

```

```

```

PROPTEST_CASES=10000
```
## Performance

- Verification time: 50-500ms per rule (SMT solving)
- Memory usage: ~50MB (Z3 context)
- Scalability: Linear in number of rules

## Limitations

- **Shift operations**: Modulo handling complex for SMT
- **Control flow**: Branch verification requires extended modeling
- **Memory operations**: Requires memory model formalization
- **Floating point**: Not yet supported

## Future Work

### Phase 1: Complete SMT Coverage

- Shift operation verification
- Control flow (branches, conditions)
- Memory operations (load/store)

### Phase 2: Optimization Verification

- DCE, constant folding, CSE correctness
- Loop optimization soundness
- Register allocation preservation

### Phase 3: Mechanized Proofs

- Port to Coq proof assistant
- Machine-checked correctness
- Certified synthesis rule library

# synth-verify - Formal Verification for Synth Compiler

Formal verification infrastructure for the Synth WebAssembly-to-ARM compiler using SMT-based translation validation.

## Overview

This crate provides:

- **SMT-based translation validation**using Z3 SMT solver
- **Formal semantics**for WebAssembly and ARM operations
- **Property-based testing**framework with proptest
- **Automated verification**of synthesis rules

## Architecture

```
synth-verify/
├── wasm_semantics.rs      # WASM → SMT encoding (25+ operations)
├── arm_semantics.rs       # ARM → SMT encoding (processor state model)
├── translation_validator.rs # Equivalence prover (Alive2-inspired)
└── properties.rs          # Property-based tests (50+ properties)
```
## Usage

### Verifying a Synthesis Rule

```
use ;
use ;
// Create Z3 context
let ctx = create_z3_context;
let validator = new;
// Define a synthesis rule

// Verify the rule
match validator.verify_rule
```
### Batch Verification

```
// Verify multiple rules

let results = validator.verify_rules;
for  in results
```
### Property-Based Testing

```
use CompilerProperties;
use *;
proptest!
```
## Verification Approach

### Translation Validation

For each synthesis rule `WASM_OP → ARM_OPS`, we prove:

```
∀inputs. ⟦WASM_OP⟧(inputs) = ⟦ARM_OPS⟧(inputs)
```
Using SMT solver:

- Create symbolic inputs
- Encode WASM semantics: `φ_wasm`
- Encode ARM semantics: `φ_arm`
- Assert: `φ_wasm ≠ φ_arm`
- Check satisfiability:
- **UNSAT**→ Proven correct
- **SAT**→ Counterexample found
- **UNKNOWN**→ Timeout

### Example: ADD Verification

```
; Symbolic inputs
(declare-const a (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-const b (_ BitVec 32))
; WASM: i32.add
(define-fun wasm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; ARM: ADD R0, R0, R1
(define-fun arm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; Prove equivalence
(assert (not (= wasm-add arm-add)))
(check-sat)  ; Returns: unsat → Proven!
```

|---|---|---|
| i32.add | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.sub | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.mul | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_s | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_u | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.and | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.or | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.xor | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.shl | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_u | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_s | ⚠ Partial | Complex |

| i32.and | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.or | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.xor | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.shl | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_u | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_s | ⚠ Partial | Complex |

## Dependencies

### Required

- **z3**- Z3 SMT solver Rust bindings (v0.12)
- **synth-synthesis**- Synthesis rules and operations
- **proptest**- Property-based testing

### System Requirements

Z3 requires either:

- System installation: `libz3-dev`or`z3`package
- Static linking: Built automatically (requires C++ compiler)

For development without Z3:

```
# Skip tests that require Z3
```
## Testing

```
# Run all tests (requires Z3)
# Run specific test suites
# Property-based testing with more cases
PROPTEST_CASES=10000
```
## Performance

- Verification time: 50-500ms per rule (SMT solving)
- Memory usage: ~50MB (Z3 context)
- Scalability: Linear in number of rules

## Limitations

- **Shift operations**: Modulo handling complex for SMT
- **Control flow**: Branch verification requires extended modeling
- **Memory operations**: Requires memory model formalization
- **Floating point**: Not yet supported

## Future Work

### Phase 1: Complete SMT Coverage

- Shift operation verification
- Control flow (branches, conditions)
- Memory operations (load/store)

### Phase 2: Optimization Verification

- DCE, constant folding, CSE correctness
- Loop optimization soundness
- Register allocation preservation

### Phase 3: Mechanized Proofs

- Port to Coq proof assistant
- Machine-checked correctness
- Certified synthesis rule library

# synth-verify - Formal Verification for Synth Compiler

Formal verification infrastructure for the Synth WebAssembly-to-ARM compiler using SMT-based translation validation.

## Overview

This crate provides:

- **SMT-based translation validation**using Z3 SMT solver
- **Formal semantics**for WebAssembly and ARM operations
- **Property-based testing**framework with proptest
- **Automated verification**of synthesis rules

## Architecture

```
synth-verify/
├── wasm_semantics.rs      # WASM → SMT encoding (25+ operations)
├── arm_semantics.rs       # ARM → SMT encoding (processor state model)
├── translation_validator.rs # Equivalence prover (Alive2-inspired)
└── properties.rs          # Property-based tests (50+ properties)
```
## Usage

### Verifying a Synthesis Rule

```
use ;
use ;
// Create Z3 context
let ctx = create_z3_context;
let validator = new;
// Define a synthesis rule
let rule = SynthesisRule ;
// Verify the rule
match validator.verify_rule
```
### Batch Verification

```
// Verify multiple rules
let rules = vec!;
let results = validator.verify_rules;
for  in results
```
### Property-Based Testing

```
use CompilerProperties;
use *;
proptest!
```
## Verification Approach

### Translation Validation

For each synthesis rule `WASM_OP → ARM_OPS`, we prove:

```
∀inputs. ⟦WASM_OP⟧(inputs) = ⟦ARM_OPS⟧(inputs)
```
Using SMT solver:

- Create symbolic inputs
- Encode WASM semantics: `φ_wasm`
- Encode ARM semantics: `φ_arm`
- Assert: `φ_wasm ≠ φ_arm`
- Check satisfiability:
- **UNSAT**→ Proven correct
- **SAT**→ Counterexample found
- **UNKNOWN**→ Timeout

### Example: ADD Verification

```
; Symbolic inputs
(declare-const a (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-const b (_ BitVec 32))
; WASM: i32.add
(define-fun wasm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; ARM: ADD R0, R0, R1
(define-fun arm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; Prove equivalence
(assert (not (= wasm-add arm-add)))
(check-sat)  ; Returns: unsat → Proven!
```
## Verified Operations

| Operation | Status | Method |
|---|---|---|
| i32.add | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.sub | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.mul | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_s | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_u | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.and | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.or | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.xor | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.shl | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_u | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_s | ⚠ Partial | Complex |

## Dependencies

### Required

- **z3**- Z3 SMT solver Rust bindings (v0.12)
- **synth-synthesis**- Synthesis rules and operations
- **proptest**- Property-based testing

### System Requirements

Z3 requires either:

- System installation: `libz3-dev`or`z3`package
- Static linking: Built automatically (requires C++ compiler)

For development without Z3:

```

```

```
# Run all tests (requires Z3)
# Run specific test suites
# Property-based testing with more cases
PROPTEST_CASES=10000
```
## Performance

- Verification time: 50-500ms per rule (SMT solving)
- Memory usage: ~50MB (Z3 context)
- Scalability: Linear in number of rules

## Limitations

- **Shift operations**: Modulo handling complex for SMT
- **Control flow**: Branch verification requires extended modeling
- **Memory operations**: Requires memory model formalization
- **Floating point**: Not yet supported

## Future Work

### Phase 1: Complete SMT Coverage

- Shift operation verification
- Control flow (branches, conditions)
- Memory operations (load/store)

### Phase 2: Optimization Verification

- DCE, constant folding, CSE correctness
- Loop optimization soundness
- Register allocation preservation

### Phase 3: Mechanized Proofs

- Port to Coq proof assistant
- Machine-checked correctness
- Certified synthesis rule library

## References

- **Alive2**: Automated LLVM verification (Lopes et al., PLDI 2021)
- **CompCert**: Verified C compiler (Leroy, POPL 2006)
- **VeriISLE**: Verified instruction selection (Nandi et al., PLDI 2020)
- **Z3**: Efficient SMT solver (de Moura & Bjørner, TACAS 2008)

## Authors

PulseEngine Team

# js_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/js-sys/^0.3.103/

## Expand description

Bindings to JavaScript’s standard, built-in objects, including their methods and properties.

This does *not* include any Web, Node, or any other JS environment
APIs. Only the things that are guaranteed to exist in the global scope by
the ECMAScript standard.

[§](https://docs.rs#a-note-about-camelcase-snake_case-and-naming-conventions)A Note About `camelCase`, `snake_case`, and Naming Conventions

JavaScript’s global objects use `camelCase` naming conventions for functions
and methods, but Rust style is to use `snake_case`. These bindings expose
the Rust style `snake_case` name. Additionally, acronyms within a method
name are all lower case, where as in JavaScript they are all upper case. For
example, `decodeURI` in JavaScript is exposed as `decode_uri` in these
bindings.

[§](https://docs.rs#a-note-about-tostring-and-to_js_string)A Note About `toString` and `to_js_string`

JavaScript’s `toString()` method is exposed as `to_js_string()` in these
bindings to avoid confusion with Rust’s [ ToString](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/trait.ToString.html) trait and its

`to_string()` method. This allows types to implement both the Rust
[trait (which provides](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html)

`Display``to_string()` via
[) and still expose the JavaScript](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/trait.ToString.html)

`ToString``toString()` functionality.## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [wasm_bindgen](https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen/0.2.126/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/wasm_bindgen/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [Atomics](https://docs.rs/Atomics/index.html)
- The `Atomics`object provides atomic operations as static methods. They are used with`SharedArrayBuffer`objects.
- [Intl](https://docs.rs/Intl/index.html)
- [JSON](https://docs.rs/JSON/index.html)
- The `JSON`object contains methods for parsing[JavaScript Object Notation (JSON)](https://json.org/)and converting values to JSON. It can’t be called or constructed, and aside from its two method properties, it has no interesting functionality of its own.
- [Math](https://docs.rs/Math/index.html)

- Bridging between JavaScript `Promise`s and Rust`Future`s.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_uri.html)- uri
- The `decodeURI()`function decodes a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) previously created by`encodeURI`or by a similar routine.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_uri_component.html)- uri_ - component
- The `decodeURIComponent()`function decodes a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) component previously created by`encodeURIComponent`or by a similar routine.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_uri.html)- uri
- The `encodeURI()`function encodes a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) by replacing each instance of certain characters by one, two, three, or four escape sequences representing the UTF-8 encoding of the character (will only be four escape sequences for characters composed of two “surrogate” characters).
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_uri_component.html)- uri_ - component
- The `encodeURIComponent()`function encodes a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) component by replacing each instance of certain characters by one, two, three, or four escape sequences representing the UTF-8 encoding of the character (will only be four escape sequences for characters composed of two “surrogate” characters).
- [escape](https://docs.rs/fn.escape.html)
- The `escape()`function computes a new string in which certain characters have been replaced by a hexadecimal escape sequence.
- [eval](https://docs.rs/fn.eval.html)
- The `eval()`function evaluates JavaScript code represented as a string.
- [global](https://docs.rs/fn.global.html)
- Returns a handle to the global scope object.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_finite.html)- finite
- The global `isFinite()`function determines whether the passed value is a finite number. If needed, the parameter is first converted to a number.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_float.html)- float
- The `parseFloat()`function parses an argument and returns a floating point number, or NaN on error.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_int.html)- int
- The `parseInt()`function parses a string argument and returns an integer of the specified radix (the base in mathematical numeral systems), or NaN on error.
- [try_](https://docs.rs/fn.try_iter.html)- iter
- Create an iterator over `val`using the JS iteration protocol and`Symbol.iterator`.
- [unescape](https://docs.rs/fn.unescape.html)
- The `unescape()`function computes a new string in which hexadecimal escape sequences are replaced with the character that it represents. The escape sequences might be introduced by a function like`escape`. Usually,`decodeURI`or`decodeURIComponent`are preferred over`unescape`.

# wasm_bindgen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen/^0.2.126/

## Expand description

Runtime support for the `wasm-bindgen` tool

This crate contains the runtime support necessary for `wasm-bindgen` the
attribute and tool. Crates pull in the `#[wasm_bindgen]` attribute through
this crate and this crate also provides JS bindings through the `JsValue`
interface.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

[§](https://docs.rs#enable-interning)`enable-interning`

Enables the internal cache for [`wasm_bindgen::intern`].

This feature currently enables the `std` feature, meaning that it is not
compatible with `no_std` environments.

[§](https://docs.rs#std-default)`std` (default)

Enabling this feature will make the crate depend on the Rust standard library.

Disable this feature to use this crate in `no_std` environments.

[§](https://docs.rs#strict-macro)`strict-macro`

All warnings the `#[wasm_bindgen]` macro emits are turned into hard errors.
This mainly affects unused attribute options.

[§](https://docs.rs#deprecated-features)Deprecated features

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-serialize)`serde-serialize`

**Deprecated:** Use the [ serde-wasm-bindgen](https://docs.rs/serde-wasm-bindgen/latest/serde_wasm_bindgen/) crate instead.

Enables the `JsValue::from_serde` and `JsValue::into_serde` methods for
serializing and deserializing Rust types to and from JavaScript.

[§](https://docs.rs#spans)`spans`

**Deprecated:** This feature became a no-op in wasm-bindgen v0.2.20 (Sep 7, 2018).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::convert::`- [IntoJsGeneric](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.IntoJsGeneric.html);
- `pub use crate::convert::`- [JsGeneric](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.JsGeneric.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [closure](https://docs.rs/closure/index.html)
- Support for closures in `wasm-bindgen`
- [convert](https://docs.rs/convert/index.html)
- ⚠️ Unstable
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- A module which is typically glob imported.
- [sys](https://docs.rs/sys/index.html)
- JavaScript system types that are re-exported by `js-sys`.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [link_to](https://docs.rs/macro.link_to.html)
- This macro takes a JS module as input and returns a URL that can be used to access it at runtime.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Clamped](https://docs.rs/struct.Clamped.html)
- A wrapper type around slices and vectors for binding the `Uint8ClampedArray`array in JS.
- [JsError](https://docs.rs/struct.JsError.html)
- Convenience type for use on exported `fn() -> Result<T, JsError>`functions, where you wish to throw a JavaScript`Error`object.
- [JsStatic](https://docs.rs/struct.JsStatic.html)- Deprecated
- Wrapper type for imported statics.
- [JsThread](https://docs.rs/struct.JsThreadLocal.html)- Local
- Wrapper type for imported statics.
- [JsValue](https://docs.rs/struct.JsValue.html)
- Representation of an object owned by JS.
- [Parent](https://docs.rs/struct.Parent.html)
- Storage wrapper for the auto-injected `parent`field on a struct that declares`#[wasm_bindgen(extends = Parent)]`.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Erasable](https://docs.rs/trait.ErasableGeneric.html)- Generic
- Private marker trait for erasable generics - types with this trait have the same repr for all generic param values, and can therefore be transmuted on the singular Repr type representation on ABI boundaries.
- [JsCast](https://docs.rs/trait.JsCast.html)
- A trait for dynamic checked and unchecked casting between JS types.
- [Unwrap](https://docs.rs/trait.UnwrapThrowExt.html)- Throw - Ext
- An extension trait for `Option<T>`and`Result<T, E>`for unwrapping the`T`value, or throwing a JS error if it is not available.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [exports](https://docs.rs/fn.exports.html)
- Returns a handle to this Wasm instance’s `WebAssembly.Instance.prototype.exports`
- [externref_](https://docs.rs/fn.externref_heap_live_count.html)- heap_ - live_ - count
- Get the count of live `externref`s /`JsValue`s in`wasm-bindgen`’s heap.
- [function_](https://docs.rs/fn.function_table.html)- table
- Returns a handle to this Wasm instance’s `WebAssembly.Table`which is the indirect function table used by Rust
- [instance](https://docs.rs/fn.instance.html)
- Returns a handle to this Wasm instance’s `WebAssembly.Instance`. This is only available when the final Wasm app is built with`--target no-modules`,`--target web`,`--target deno`or`--target nodejs`. It is unavailable for`--target bundler`.
- [intern](https://docs.rs/fn.intern.html)
- Interns Rust strings so that it’s much faster to send them to JS.
- [memory](https://docs.rs/fn.memory.html)
- Returns a handle to this Wasm instance’s `WebAssembly.Memory`
- [module](https://docs.rs/fn.module.html)
- Returns a handle to this Wasm instance’s `WebAssembly.Module`. This is only available when the final Wasm app is built with`--target no-modules`,`--target web`,`--target deno`or`--target nodejs`. It is unavailable for`--target bundler`.
- [throw_](https://docs.rs/fn.throw_str.html)- str
- Throws a JS exception.
- [throw_](https://docs.rs/fn.throw_val.html)- val
- Rethrow a JS exception
- [unintern](https://docs.rs/fn.unintern.html)
- Removes a Rust string from the intern cache.

# euv_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/euv-core/0.8.15/target-redirect/euv_core/

## Expand description

euv

A declarative, cross-platform UI framework for Rust with virtual DOM, reactive signals, and HTML macros for WebAssembly.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Attr](https://docs.rs/struct.AttrValueAdapter.html)- Value - Adapter
- Adapts an arbitrary attribute value expression into an `AttributeValue`.
- [Attribute](https://docs.rs/struct.AttributeEntry.html)- Entry
- Represents a single attribute on a virtual DOM node.
- [Callback](https://docs.rs/struct.CallbackNamedAdapter.html)- Named - Adapter
- Adapts a callback with a custom name into an `AttributeValue`.
- [Css](https://docs.rs/struct.Css.html)
- Represents a CSS class with a name, its style declarations, and optional pseudo rules.
- [Dynamic](https://docs.rs/struct.DynamicNode.html)- Node
- A closure-based dynamic node that re-renders when its dependency signals change.
- [Event](https://docs.rs/struct.EventAdapter.html)- Adapter
- Adapts various event value types into an `AttributeValue`for event attributes.
- [Event](https://docs.rs/struct.EventNamedAdapter.html)- Named - Adapter
- Adapts an event with a specific event name into an `AttributeValue`.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/struct.HookContext.html)- Context
- Manages hook state across render cycles for a DynamicNode.
- [Interval](https://docs.rs/struct.IntervalHandle.html)- Handle
- A handle to a browser interval timer created by `use_interval`.
- [Media](https://docs.rs/struct.MediaRule.html)- Rule
- Represents a CSS @media rule attached to a class.
- [Native](https://docs.rs/struct.NativeEventHandler.html)- Event - Handler
- A wrapper around an event callback.
- [Pseudo](https://docs.rs/struct.PseudoRule.html)- Rule
- Represents a CSS pseudo-class or pseudo-element rule attached to a class.
- [Signal](https://docs.rs/struct.Signal.html)
- A reactive signal handle.
- [Signal](https://docs.rs/struct.SignalCell.html)- Cell
- A `Sync`wrapper for single-threaded global`Signal`access.
- [Text](https://docs.rs/struct.TextNode.html)- Node
- Represents a text node in the virtual DOM.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Attribute](https://docs.rs/enum.AttributeValue.html)- Value
- Represents the value of an HTML attribute.
- [Tag](https://docs.rs/enum.Tag.html)
- Represents the type of an HTML tag or a component.
- [Virtual](https://docs.rs/enum.VirtualNode.html)- Node
- Represents a node in the virtual DOM tree.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [batch](https://docs.rs/fn.batch.html)
- Batches signal updates within a closure, deferring DOM dispatch until the outermost batch completes.
- [mount](https://docs.rs/fn.mount.html)
- Mounts the given virtual DOM tree to a specific element matched by a CSS selector.
- [schedule_](https://docs.rs/fn.schedule_update.html)- update
- Schedules a deferred signal update with precise dirty marking.
- [use_](https://docs.rs/fn.use_cleanup.html)- cleanup
- Registers a cleanup callback that will be executed when the current
hook context is cleared (e.g., when a `match`arm switches).
- [use_](https://docs.rs/fn.use_interval.html)- interval
- Creates a recurring interval that invokes the given closure at the
specified period, returning an `IntervalHandle`that is automatically cleared when the hook context is cleared (i.e., when the component unmounts or a`match`arm switches).
- [use_](https://docs.rs/fn.use_signal.html)- signal
- Creates a new reactive signal with the given initial value.
- [use_](https://docs.rs/fn.use_window_event.html)- window_ - event
- Registers a `window.addEventListener`callback using event delegation, automatically removed when the hook context is cleared.

# AttrValueAdapter in euv_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/euv-core/0.8.15/euv_core/struct.AttrValueAdapter.html

`pub struct AttrValueAdapter<T> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Adapts an arbitrary attribute value expression into an `AttributeValue`.

Handles the dispatch between event closures and reactive values without
requiring the macro to generate inline trait hierarchies. The macro emits
`AttrValueAdapter::new(expr).into_attribute_value()` instead of the
`__IsClosure` / `__ClosurePicker` / `__ValuePicker` / `__FallbackHelper`
/ `__dispatch` boilerplate.

For event attributes (key starts with “on”), event closures are wrapped
into `AttributeValue::Event`. For non-event attributes, values are
converted via `IntoReactiveValue`.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Adapts a `FnMut(Event)` closure into a callback `AttributeValue`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/cast/impl.rs.html#359-385)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-AttrValueAdapter%3CF%3E)

### impl<F> [AttrValueAdapter](https://docs.rs/struct.AttrValueAdapter.html)<F>

Adapts a `FnMut(Event)` closure into a callback `AttributeValue`.

This handles the case where a closure is used as a component callback prop.
The closure is converted via `IntoCallbackAttribute::into_callback_attribute()`.

# DynamicNode in euv_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/euv-core/0.8.15/euv_core/struct.DynamicNode.html

`pub struct DynamicNode { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A closure-based dynamic node that re-renders when its dependency signals change.

Holds a shared reference to a heap-allocated render closure that produces a fresh
`VirtualNode` on each evaluation. The renderer subscribes to the closure’s
signals and patches the DOM automatically.
Contains a `HookContext` that persists hook state (like `use_signal`) across
re-renders, ensuring that signal values are not reset when the render function
is called again.

Uses `Rc<UnsafeCell<>>` instead of `Rc<RefCell<>>` to avoid runtime borrow
checking overhead. Safety is guaranteed by the single-threaded WASM context.
The `Rc` provides automatic memory management — the render closure is freed
when the last reference (either in the VirtualNode tree or the signal update
callback) is dropped.

# EventAdapter in euv_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/euv-core/0.8.15/euv_core/struct.EventAdapter.html

`pub struct EventAdapter<T> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Adapts various event value types into an `AttributeValue` for event attributes.

The `html!` macro generates `EventAdapter::new(expr).into_attribute(event_name)`
instead of inline trait dispatch boilerplate. This eliminates the per-attribute-site
generation of `__EventWrapper`, `__IsClosure`, `__ClosurePicker`, `__ValuePicker`,
`__FallbackHelper`, and `__dispatch` types, significantly reducing macro output size.

The adapter pattern handles three cases:

- `FnMut(NativeEvent)`closure →- `AttributeValue::Event`via- `NativeEventHandler`
- `NativeEventHandler`directly →- `AttributeValue::Event`as-is
- `Option<NativeEventHandler>`→- `AttributeValue::Event`or- `AttributeValue::Text`

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/cast/impl.rs.html#190-206)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-EventAdapter%3CF%3E)### impl<F> [EventAdapter](https://docs.rs/struct.EventAdapter.html)<F>

Adapts a `FnMut(Event)` closure into an `AttributeValue::Event`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/cast/impl.rs.html#190-206)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-EventAdapter%3CF%3E)

### impl<F> [EventAdapter](https://docs.rs/struct.EventAdapter.html)<F>

Adapts a `FnMut(Event)` closure into an `AttributeValue::Event`.

Wraps the closure into a `NativeEventHandler` and returns it as an
event attribute value. This replaces the `__EventWrapper<F>` type
that was previously generated inline by the `html!` macro.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/cast/impl.rs.html#270-288)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-EventAdapter%3CNativeEventHandler%3E)Adapts an owned `NativeEventHandler` into an `AttributeValue::Event` directly.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/cast/impl.rs.html#270-288)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-EventAdapter%3CNativeEventHandler%3E)

Adapts an owned `NativeEventHandler` into an `AttributeValue::Event` directly.

When the user already provides a `NativeEventHandler`, the handler is
re-wrapped with the given `event_name` to ensure the DOM event listener
is bound to the correct event type (e.g., “click” rather than “onclick”).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/cast/impl.rs.html#283-287)#### pub fn [into_attribute](https://docs.rs#method.into_attribute-1)(self, event_name: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [AttributeValue](https://docs.rs/enum.AttributeValue.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/cast/impl.rs.html#283-287)

#### pub fn [into_attribute](https://docs.rs#method.into_attribute-1)(self, event_name: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [AttributeValue](https://docs.rs/enum.AttributeValue.html)

Converts the wrapped handler into an event `AttributeValue`.

Re-wraps the handler with the provided `event_name` so that the
DOM event listener uses the correct event type string.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-1)Arguments

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-1)Returns

- `AttributeValue`- An- `AttributeValue::Event`containing the re-wrapped handler.

Adapts an `Option<NativeEventHandler>` into an `AttributeValue`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/cast/impl.rs.html#294-313)

### impl [EventAdapter](https://docs.rs/struct.EventAdapter.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[NativeEventHandler](https://docs.rs/struct.NativeEventHandler.html)>>

Adapts an `Option<NativeEventHandler>` into an `AttributeValue`.

`Some(handler)` becomes `AttributeValue::Event(handler)` re-wrapped with the
given event name, and `None` becomes `AttributeValue::Text(String::new())`.

Adapts an `Option<Rc<dyn Fn(Event)>>` into an `AttributeValue`.

`Some(callback)` becomes `AttributeValue::Event` by wrapping the shared closure
into a `NativeEventHandler`, and `None` becomes `AttributeValue::Text(String::new())`.
This supports component Props that use `Option<Rc<dyn Fn(Event)>>` for event callbacks.

# EventNamedAdapter in euv_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/euv-core/0.8.15/euv_core/struct.EventNamedAdapter.html

`pub struct EventNamedAdapter<T> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Adapts an event with a specific event name into an `AttributeValue`.

This type wraps an event value and its event name, enabling
`Into<AttributeValue>` trait implementation for events.
Used by the `html!` macro for event attributes like `onclick`.

Converts an event named adapter with optional shared closure into an `AttributeValue`.

`Some(callback)` becomes `AttributeValue::Event` by wrapping the shared closure
into a `NativeEventHandler` with the adapter’s event name, and `None` becomes
`AttributeValue::Text(String::new())`.

# HookContext in euv_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/euv-core/0.8.15/euv_core/struct.HookContext.html

`pub struct HookContext { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Manages hook state across render cycles for a DynamicNode.

Stores boxed `Any` values keyed by hook call order, enabling `use_signal`
and similar hooks to persist state between re-renders of the same
dynamic node.

Implements `Clone` for ergonomic use; all clones share the same underlying state.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/reactive/hook/impl.rs.html#9-13)

#### pub fn [reset_index](https://docs.rs#method.reset_index)(&mut self)

Resets the hook index for a new render cycle.

Sets the internal hook index back to zero so that subsequent
`use_signal` calls start indexing from the beginning of the hook list.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/reactive/hook/impl.rs.html#24-43)#### pub fn [switch_arm](https://docs.rs#method.switch_arm)(&mut self, changed: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/reactive/hook/impl.rs.html#24-43)

#### pub fn [switch_arm](https://docs.rs#method.switch_arm)(&mut self, changed: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

Notifies the hook context that a match arm is being entered.

If the arm index has changed, all existing hooks and cleanups are cleared and re-initialized for the new arm. If the arm is unchanged, only the hook index is reset.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `usize`- The index of the new match arm.

# NativeEventHandler in euv_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/euv-core/0.8.15/euv_core/struct.NativeEventHandler.html

`pub struct NativeEventHandler { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A wrapper around an event callback.

Stores the event name and a shared reference to the callback closure.
Uses `Rc<UnsafeCell<>>` instead of `Rc<RefCell<>>` to avoid runtime
borrow checking overhead in the single-threaded WASM context.
The `Rc` provides automatic memory management (freed when last reference drops).

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/reactive/cast/impl.rs.html#143-152)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-From%3CNativeEventHandler%3E-for-AttributeValue)### impl [From](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)<[NativeEventHandler](https://docs.rs/struct.NativeEventHandler.html)> for [AttributeValue](https://docs.rs/enum.AttributeValue.html)

Converts an owned event handler into a callback attribute value.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/reactive/cast/impl.rs.html#143-152)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-From%3CNativeEventHandler%3E-for-AttributeValue)

### impl [From](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)<[NativeEventHandler](https://docs.rs/struct.NativeEventHandler.html)> for [AttributeValue](https://docs.rs/enum.AttributeValue.html)

Converts an owned event handler into a callback attribute value.

Re-wraps the handler with a generic “callback” event name so that
subsequent `EventAdapter::into_attribute` calls can override it with
the correct DOM event type.

# Signal in euv_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/euv-core/0.8.15/euv_core/struct.Signal.html

`pub struct Signal<T>{ /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A reactive signal handle.

Allows reading, writing, and subscribing to changes.
Implements `Clone` and `Copy` for ergonomic use; all copies share the same
underlying state. The inner state is heap-allocated via `Box` and accessed
through a raw pointer stored as a `usize`. The allocation is tracked in a
global registry for lifecycle management. The `Copy` semantics are safe
because only the pointer address is copied — the actual heap allocation
is owned by the registry.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Creates a new `Signal` with the given initial value.

Allocates `SignalInner<T>` on the heap via `Box`, stores the raw pointer
address, and registers it in the global registry for lifecycle tracking.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `T`- The initial value of the signal.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns)Returns

- `Self`- A handle to the newly created reactive signal.

Returns the current value of the signal.

Directly reads the value from the heap-allocated inner state via raw pointer dereference. No runtime borrow checking overhead.

If the signal has been marked inactive (`alive == false`), returns the
last stored value without registering tracking dependencies. This
ensures that stale async callbacks (e.g., orphaned `setInterval`)
holding a `Signal` copy can still call `.get()` safely without
triggering side effects or panics.

If a tracking context is active (i.e., a DynamicNode is being rendered), automatically registers the current dynamic node as a dependent of this signal for precise reactive updates.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-1)Returns

- `T`- The current value of the signal.

Sets the value of the signal and notifies listeners.

Uses precise dirty marking: only dynamic nodes that depend on this signal are marked dirty, avoiding full broadcast.

When called inside `batch`, the dispatch is
deferred (dirty slots are still marked precisely), and the
outermost `set()` call outside the suppressed scope will
trigger the actual dispatch cycle.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-2)Arguments

- `T`- The new value to assign to the signal.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/reactive/signal/impl.rs.html#267)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Copy-for-Signal%3CT%3E)

Copies the signal, sharing the same inner state.

Safe because only the inner address (a `usize`) is copied;
the actual heap allocation is owned by the global signal registry.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/reactive/signal/struct.rs.html#65)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Eq-for-Signal%3CT%3E)

Converts a mutable bool signal into a reactive attribute value.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/reactive/cast/impl.rs.html#43-52)

# AttributeValue in euv_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/euv-core/0.8.15/euv_core/enum.AttributeValue.html

```
pub enum AttributeValue {
    Text(
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)),
    Signal([Signal](https://docs.rs/struct.Signal.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>),
    Event([NativeEventHandler](https://docs.rs/struct.NativeEventHandler.html)),

}## Expand description

Represents the value of an HTML attribute.

Attributes can be static text, reactive signals, event handlers, dynamic expressions, or CSS class references.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Dynamic)

A dynamic expression value of any type (for component props).

A CSS class reference created by the `class!` macro.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/attribute/impl.rs.html#7-138)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-AttributeValue)### impl [AttributeValue](https://docs.rs/enum.AttributeValue.html)

Implementation of attribute value factory methods for reactive and merged values.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/attribute/impl.rs.html#7-138)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-AttributeValue)

### impl [AttributeValue](https://docs.rs/enum.AttributeValue.html)

Implementation of attribute value factory methods for reactive and merged values.

Creates a reactive attribute `Self` for conditional attribute values.

This function replaces the inline `Signal::create(...)` + `subscribe_attr(...)`
boilerplate that was previously generated by the `html!` macro for every
attribute value containing an `if` condition.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `Fn() -> String + 'static`- A closure that computes the current attribute value. Called on initial render and whenever any signal changes.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns)Returns

- `Self`- A- `Self::Signal`backed by a- `Signal<String>`that reactively re-evaluates the attribute value on signal updates.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/attribute/impl.rs.html#47-88)#### pub fn [merge_class](https://docs.rs#method.merge_class)(values: &[Self]) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/attribute/impl.rs.html#47-88)

#### pub fn [merge_class](https://docs.rs#method.merge_class)(values: &[Self]) -> Self

Merges multiple class attribute values into a single `Self`.

Each input value is adapted into a `Self` via `IntoReactiveValue`.
`Css` values are injected into the DOM and their names are collected.
All non-empty class names are joined with spaces into a final `Text` attribute.
If any value is signal-backed, the result becomes a reactive `Signal` attribute
that re-evaluates when any constituent signal changes.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-1)Arguments

- `&[Self]`- The class attribute values to merge.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-1)Returns

- `Self`- A merged attribute value containing space-separated class names.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/attribute/impl.rs.html#104-137)#### pub fn [merge_style](https://docs.rs#method.merge_style)(values: &[Self]) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/attribute/impl.rs.html#104-137)

#### pub fn [merge_style](https://docs.rs#method.merge_style)(values: &[Self]) -> Self

Merges multiple style attribute values into a single `Self`.

Each input value is expected to be a style string (`Text`) or a reactive
`Signal<String>` producing a style string. All non-empty style strings are
joined with spaces into a final combined style attribute.
If any value is signal-backed, the result becomes a reactive `Signal` attribute.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments-2)Arguments

- `&[Self]`- The style attribute values to merge.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-2)Returns

- `Self`- A merged attribute value containing the combined CSS style string.

Converts an event named adapter with optional shared closure into an `AttributeValue`.

`Some(callback)` becomes `AttributeValue::Event` by wrapping the shared closure
into a `NativeEventHandler` with the adapter’s event name, and `None` becomes
`AttributeValue::Text(String::new())`.

The signal is mapped to a `Signal<String>` that yields `"true"` or `"false"`,
enabling boolean attributes like `checked` to reactively update the DOM.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/attribute/impl.rs.html#149-179)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-PartialEq-for-AttributeValue)### impl [PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialEq.html) for [AttributeValue](https://docs.rs/enum.AttributeValue.html)

Visual equality comparison for attribute values.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/attribute/impl.rs.html#149-179)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-PartialEq-for-AttributeValue)

### impl [PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialEq.html) for [AttributeValue](https://docs.rs/enum.AttributeValue.html)

Visual equality comparison for attribute values.

Compares values by their visual output rather than identity. `Signal`
values are compared by their current resolved string; when both signals
share the same inner pointer, they are always considered **unequal**
because the signal may have mutated between VDOM snapshots and `.get()`
would return the same current value for both, masking the change.
`Event` values are always considered equal (re-binding is handled by the
handler registry), and `Css` values are compared by class name.

# VirtualNode in euv_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/euv-core/0.8.15/euv_core/enum.VirtualNode.html

`pub enum VirtualNode<T = `[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)> {
    Element {
        tag: [Tag](https://docs.rs/enum.Tag.html),
        attributes: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[AttributeEntry](https://docs.rs/struct.AttributeEntry.html)>,
        children: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[VirtualNode](https://docs.rs/enum.VirtualNode.html)>,
        key: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
        props: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<T>>,
    },
    Text([TextNode](https://docs.rs/struct.TextNode.html)),
    Fragment([Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[VirtualNode](https://docs.rs/enum.VirtualNode.html)>),
    Dynamic([DynamicNode](https://docs.rs/struct.DynamicNode.html)),
    Empty,
}## Expand description

Represents a node in the virtual DOM tree.

The core enum representing elements, text, fragments, and empty nodes.
The generic parameter `T` carries the component props type for component nodes.
For non-component nodes, `T` defaults to `()`.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Element)

### Element

An element node with a tag, attributes, children, and optional props.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Text)

### Text([TextNode](https://docs.rs/struct.TextNode.html))

A text node containing string content and an optional reactive signal.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Fragment)

### Fragment([Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[VirtualNode](https://docs.rs/enum.VirtualNode.html)>)

A fragment of multiple nodes without a wrapper element.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Dynamic)

### Dynamic([DynamicNode](https://docs.rs/struct.DynamicNode.html))

A dynamic node that re-renders based on signal changes.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Empty)

### Empty

An empty placeholder node.

`Some(vec)` converts the vector into a `VirtualNode::Fragment` (or `Empty`
if the vector is empty), `None` returns `VirtualNode::Empty`.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-9)Returns

- `VirtualNode`- A- `VirtualNode::Fragment`if- `Some`with nodes,- `VirtualNode::Empty`if- `None`or the vector is empty.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/node/impl.rs.html#82-130)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-PartialEq-for-VirtualNode%3CT%3E)### impl<T: [PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialEq.html)> [PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialEq.html) for [VirtualNode](https://docs.rs/enum.VirtualNode.html)<T>

Visual equality comparison for virtual DOM nodes.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/euv_core/vdom/node/impl.rs.html#82-130)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-PartialEq-for-VirtualNode%3CT%3E)

### impl<T: [PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialEq.html)> [PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialEq.html) for [VirtualNode](https://docs.rs/enum.VirtualNode.html)<T>

Visual equality comparison for virtual DOM nodes.

Used by DynamicNode re-rendering to skip unnecessary DOM patches when the rendered output has not changed. Event attributes are always considered equal because re-binding event listeners is handled separately by the handler registry and does not affect visual output. Dynamic nodes manage their own subtree re-rendering, so two Dynamic variants are always considered equal — the inner renderer handles patching when the dynamic content actually changes.
